actions: Add the missing first-party loopback MCP Policy Enforcement transport required by ADR-0001
Keep mandatory tools/call policy enforcement inside src-tauri/src/mcp rather than moving raw MCP into LB-009 app/runtime code
Preserve downstream MCP initialize/session/tools-list/tools-call semantics while using the already authenticated CodingToolsRuntime hop
Preserve downstream JSON-RPC request IDs on upstream tools/call so pinned coding-tools-mcp cancellation semantics remain valid
Accept bounded concurrent downstream HTTP connections while serializing guarded tool execution and forwarding notifications/cancelled outside the Guard execution mutex
Add actual bundled coding-tools-mcp regressions proving cached-mode bypass prevention, real forwarding, reverse ownership recovery, and cancellation of a long-running command
Allow orderly PEP stop to return the owned CodingToolsRuntime so LB-009 can enforce Tunnel then PEP then MCP shutdown
records.reason: LB-009 composition audit proved LB-007 had only an in-process McpGuard and no production listener, while LB-008 TunnelRuntime always targets 127.0.0.1:<mcp_guard_port>/mcp. Without this correction the runtime could report staged readiness while the configured PEP endpoint did not exist.
records.evidence_ref: Current-disk search during LB-009: McpGuard::new existed only in tests and no production PEP TcpListener existed; ADR-0001 requires Tunnel -> loopback Rust MCP Guard/PEP -> authenticated coding-tools-mcp. Pinned coding-tools-mcp v0.2.2 uses ThreadingHTTPServer, supports notifications/cancelled, and maps JSON-RPC request_id to exec sessions; tunnel-client v0.0.11 allows concurrent MCP requests. Deterministic Windows regression with actual bundled coding-tools-mcp proved a 10-second exec_command can be cancelled through the new PEP on a second downstream connection using the same request id while CurrentTask returns to Idle.
